Crisp exquisite surface detail and strong material depth, restrained luminosity, no huge halo, no fog, no floating debris. Asymmetric concept: MASSIVE BROAD CRESCENT UPPER LIMB versus a VERY LONG THIN LOWER LIMB. The upper section is one large sculpted cobalt crescent, its open bite visible, about twice the width of anything below the grip; its upper hooked tip curls inward. Place the grip somewhat above the bow's overall vertical midpoint. The lower limb extends much farther down as a spare elegant tapering blue-moonlight reed with one gentle S-bend and a tiny recurved endpoint. The lower half must NOT have a second matching crescent, fan, wing or bulky ornament. Contrasting compact heavy crescent above and stretched graceful fine line below is the defining silhouette.
